vuln_id: ARVO arvo:66311 / S2OPC Variant builtInTypeId off-by-one

bug_description.original: An out-of-bounds access occurs in the builtintype tables, potentially leading to security issues.
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json issue_description / patch.diff / sanitizer_trace.txt / reproduction_report.json / staged vulnerable source snapshot / staged poc
bug_description.normalized: The staged 2-byte witness `a6 da` makes the harness choose `SOPC_KnownEncodeableTypes[166] == LiteralOperand`, whose only field is a `SOPC_Variant`. `SOPC_Variant_Read_Internal()` then reads `0xda` as the Variant encoding byte, interprets it as a matrix Variant with `builtInTypeId = 26`, and calls `ReadVariantArrayBuiltInType()`. The vulnerable read-side bounds check wrongly accepts `SOPC_BUILTINID_MAX + 1`; `getBuiltinOptimizableSize()` therefore leaves `eltOptimSize == 0`, and the generic array path indexes `SOPC_BuiltInType_HandlingTable[26]` / `SOPC_BuiltInType_EncodingTable[26]` one entry past the `[SOPC_BUILTINID_MAX + 1]` tables. AddressSanitizer reports the first out-of-bounds read at `src/Common/opcua_types/sopc_encoder.c:2610`.

source.description: First project-code parser step on the vulnerable path that consumes the remaining attacker-controlled payload byte and materializes it as the Variant encoding byte.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` is exactly two bytes `a6 da`. In the harness, `0xa6 % SOPC_TypeInternalIndex_SIZE == 166`, so `SOPC_KnownEncodeableTypes[166]` is `LiteralOperand` and the attached decode buffer is the single remaining byte `0xda`. This statement reads that byte into `encodingByte`, from which the later array flags and built-in type id are derived.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer crash site. With `builtInTypeId == 26`, evaluating the first size argument reads `SOPC_BuiltInType_HandlingTable[26]` one entry past the 26-element global table; the same call also prepares two more one-past-end table lookups from the encoding and initialize/clear tables.
sink.note: ASan reports `READ of size 8` at `src/Common/opcua_types/sopc_encoder.c:2610:80`, which lands on the `.size` read from `SOPC_BuiltInType_HandlingTable`.

root_cause.description: Root cause. The read-side bounds check accepts `builtInTypeId == SOPC_BUILTINID_MAX + 1` even though `SOPC_BuiltinId` ends at 25 and the built-in handling/encoding tables only have valid indices 0..25. The fix tightens this guard to `> SOPC_BUILTINID_MAX`.

parser_admitted.description: Project-side admission point into the vulnerable parser. For the harness-selected `LiteralOperand`, `LiteralOperand_Fields[0]` is a built-in `SOPC_Variant_Id`, so this dispatch calls the Variant decoder on the single remaining payload byte.
parser_admitted.note: The first witness byte selects `LiteralOperand`; the second byte remains unread until this dispatch reaches `SOPC_Variant_Read_Internal()`.

tainted_value_origin.description: The low 6 bits of the attacker-controlled Variant encoding byte become the exact built-in type id later consumed as a table index.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: For the staged witness byte `0xda`, masking with `0x3f` yields `26`, i.e. `SOPC_BUILTINID_MAX + 1`.

coarse_trace.summary: The first PoC byte `0xa6` selects `SOPC_KnownEncodeableTypes[166] == LiteralOperand`; the remaining byte `0xda` becomes the decode buffer.
LiteralOperand's only field descriptor is a built-in Variant, so the generic object decoder dispatches into `SOPC_Variant_Read_Internal()`.
The Variant decoder interprets `0xda` as a matrix Variant encoding byte, deriving `BuiltInTypeId = 26` and calling `ReadVariantArrayBuiltInType()`.
The off-by-one range check accepts 26, `eltOptimSize` remains 0, and the generic array path overreads the built-in handling table at line 2610.

fine_trace.note: Source. The Variant decoder reads the only remaining payload byte into `encodingByte`; for the staged witness this byte is `0xda`, which later supplies both the array/dimensions flags and the built-in type id.
Because both `SOPC_VariantArrayValueFlag` and `SOPC_VariantArrayDimensionsFlag` are set in `0xda`, the Variant is classified as a matrix and the array-value decoder becomes reachable.
Masking off the two high flag bits turns `0xda` into `26`, the one-past-end built-in type id later used as a table index.
When `ReadVariantArrayBuiltInType()` receives `builtInTypeId == 26`, this range check evaluates false instead of rejecting the value, so decoding continues with an out-of-range id.
The helper is called with the same out-of-range id 26. Because 26 is not any optimized scalar case, it returns `0`, leaving the generic table-driven decode path selected.

This predicate is false because step 5 produced `eltOptimSize == 0`, so execution skips the optimized flat-buffer path and falls into the generic `SOPC_Read_Array()` call that dereferences the built-in tables.

With `builtInTypeId == 26` and the generic path selected, evaluating the first size argument reads `SOPC_BuiltInType_HandlingTable[26].size` one entry past the 26-element global table. ASan reports this exact read as the `READ of size 8` at line 2610.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: The bundled patch changes the read-side and helper guards from `> SOPC_BUILTINID_MAX + 1` to `> SOPC_BUILTINID_MAX`, which would reject the witness-derived `builtInTypeId == 26` before the table lookup at line 2610. Stage 02 did not dynamically validate the fixed image.

poc.trigger: The staged witness is exactly two bytes `a6 da`. `0xa6` selects `SOPC_KnownEncodeableTypes[166] == LiteralOperand` in the fuzzer harness, leaving one payload byte. `SOPC_Variant_Read_Internal()` then reads `0xda` as the LiteralOperand's Variant encoding byte, interprets it as a matrix Variant with `builtInTypeId = 26`, and reaches the out-of-bounds built-in table read in `ReadVariantArrayBuiltInType()`.

format.name: 2-byte decode_fuzzer input selecting LiteralOperand with invalid Variant encoding byte
format.contract: The verified trigger is the exact staged 2-byte witness `a6 da`: the first byte must select `LiteralOperand` (`0xa6 % SOPC_TypeInternalIndex_SIZE == 166` in this build), and the second byte must be `0xda`, i.e. both Variant array flags set plus low 6 bits equal to `26`. On the staged vulnerable path, that exact combination makes `SOPC_Variant_Read_Internal()` derive `builtInTypeId == SOPC_BUILTINID_MAX + 1`, after which `ReadVariantArrayBuiltInType()` accepts the value and evaluates `SOPC_BuiltInType_HandlingTable[26].size` out of bounds. Stage 02 verified only this exact witness shape, not a generalized class of other type-selector or encoding-byte combinations.

evidence_note: This Stage 02 GT is grounded in the staged vulnerable S2OPC checkout, the saved AddressSanitizer crash traces, the staged patch diff, `reproduction_report.json`, and direct inspection of the staged 2-byte PoC.
evidence_limitations: Stage 02 did not rebuild or rerun anything beyond the saved Stage 01 evidence.
No fixed-image dynamic validation was performed here; patch relevance is source-grounded from `patch.diff`.
Runtime disambiguation remained disabled (`run_flags.json` sets `runtime_disambiguation` to false), so no instrumentation was added.
